notes.title: Bugfixes and Big News
notes.notes:
[b]Ahoy, you![/b]

It's been a while (as ever) since last we spoke, but I have news aplenty.

[b]Firstly:[/b]
Many of you may know that I've spent a decent chunk of the past few years working on [b]UFO 50[/b]. Which is finished now! Hooray! You should definitely [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1147860/UFO_50/]go play it[/url] if you haven't yet: It's a wonderful game and I'm very proud of the work that I and the rest of the UFO 50 Recovery Team did on it.

So, now that I'm finished with my work on UFO 50, what does the future hold for Catacomb Kids?

Well that brings me to the second and more relevant bit of news:

[b]I started a game company![/b]

Catacomb Kids composer Stevie and I have teamed up to form [url=https://oddobject.zone]Odd Object[/url]. I'm super stoked! But more than just stoked, this move opens up a number of opportunities for me to grow and evolve as a game dev.

This has a couple implications for the future of Catacomb Kids:
[olist][*] We're working on our studio's first game, which will result in another lull in CK updates as we put together something new. We have an ambitiously short development time for this new project though, so my attention will only be turned away for a short while. I can't talk much about it just yet but I'm excited to share more details soon.
[*] Once that project is launched I plan to return my focus to Catacomb Kids along with a wealth of new resources and an intensity of attention that I haven't had the ability to muster in many long years. The intention then will be to push the game - finally - to 1.0.[/olist]
Part of the decision to start this company has been to ensure that I have a stable plan for myself and my work that allows me to properly support CK's development long-term.

In the meantime, this most recent 0.2.4 update is intended to iron out many of the most egregious outstanding bugs and crashes with the game so that you all can continue to enjoy it until I can once more give the game my full attention as it deserves.

I thank you all for your trust and time thus far, and truly appreciate your support and what you've invested in Catacomb Kids.

We shall speak again erelong!
- Tyriq (aka. FourbitFriday)

notes.title: 0.2.11 Patch Notes
notes.notes:
Happy (just-about) New Year! 

Here's hoping 2022 sees the world in a better place than 2021. Fingers crossed!

But at the very least, to round out this year (aka. "2020: Part 2"), have a Catacomb Kids update.
(Just on Windows for now: Mac + Linux following in a few days.)

[b][h2]0.2.11[/h2][/b]
It's not the Deep Dark yet, but it [i]is[/i] a bunch of bugfixes!

The Deep Dark update should be out probably sometime early next spring. It's very nearly done in terms of content, but still needs a big audio pass and some finessing of certain edge cases in the level generation. Once the Deep Dark is released, I'll get started working on the fourth - and final - area: The Mad Hell!

But that's all still in the future! In the meantime, here's the patch notes for this update. Most significantly, I've added a shortcut system, whereby activating a [i]certain machine[/i] that occasionally appears in the Anticropolis will thereafter on every subsequent run spawn a shortcut between the Upper Dungeon and Anticropolis. It won't be a free trip though; the shortcut entrance is hidden, and guarded by tough enemies.

notes.notes:
Hey, remember me? Have an update!

I'm hard at work on the [b]Deep Dark[/b], and it's coming along quite nicely but isn't quite ready for public consumption yet, so I wanted to push out some bugfixes and tweaks that I think will make the game a bit smoother and more fun.

In this update are [b]mirror-and-laser[/b] puzzles that now spawn in the Anticropolis, acting as the AC's version of switch barriers. There are also [b]frozen passages[/b] that must be broken through in order to traverse, and which slowly close up behind you, as well as a number of fixes for major crashes and long-standing bugs. 

Also by popular request an option has been added for [b]splitscreen-only mode[/b] in Co-op, which you can enable in Options > Gameplay.

New
[list][*] Laser-and-Mirror locks in the Anticropolis
[*] Frozen passages in the Anticropolis

notes.title: Level Generator Update 0.2.0! And Some Other Stuff!!
notes.notes:
Hey! 
Here's a video:
[h1][b][url=https://youtu.be/dS6pb-QEnU8]Catacomb Kids - Level Gen Update 0.2.0 Vlog![/url][/b][/h1]

If you don't want to watch that here are the same words below, followed by some extra words:

I know it's been a long time since the last update. There are a lot of reasons for that, but to keep things short, it's because I'm much busier now than I was before - in a good way, working on [b]UFO 50[/b] with Derek Yu and Paul Hubans and a couple other Super Rad Dudes - and because I was working very very hard on rewriting a pretty fundamental part of the game. Namely: the level generator.
So, here, have an update.

[h1]The Generator[/h1]
The aforementioned rewritten level generator can now produce [b]proper lock-and-key situations[/b], or switch-and-gate situations, or switch-and-furnace situations, or whatever other kinds of "need to get X to go to Y" kinds of scenarios I decide to add in the future. The new generator also features many, many other tweaks to the levels that are probably less immediately obvious but no less impactful. There are also a [b]boatload of new premade[/b] rooms that take advantage of some fun things now possible in the new level generator. I finally made myself a proper editor for making premade rooms that makes the process significantly faster and less of a headache than it was before, so just about every update from now on will probably feature some new premade rooms and setpieces to some degree or another.

[h1]The Rewards[/h1]
While I was making all those fancy new premade rooms, I realized that there weren't enough things I could use as general reward type items other than Fancy Chests, so I added a few!
[list]
[*]There are now [b]Soul Chests[/b], which are special treasure chests that power up by consuming the corpses of nearby slain enemies. The more corpses they consume, the better the loot they drop will be!
[*]In addition, you can now find extra [b]learning points and free spells[/b] just floating around sometimes.
[*]I've also added a new kind of item called "[b]Blessings[/b]", which are permanent passive powerups, sort of like never-ending trances but a bit less potent. You can only have one blessing at a time though, so choose wisely. There are only three implemented currently but more are definitely on the way.
[/list]
[h1]The Boons[/h1]
I've also added four new leveling boons, two STR and two SPD.
[list]
[*][b]Weapon Master[/b] lets you use any weapon skill that you have access to with any weapon regardless of its type.
[*][b]Living Weapon[/b] lets you use weapon skills while unarmed and removes the damage penalty on unarmed attacks. When you first learn it, it forces you to pick a weapon class to hate, but you then gain that weapon class' full moveset as unarmed attacks.
[*][b]Breakthrough[/b] lets you charge up a super-jump to launch high into the air, bust through single-tile-thick walls and ceilings, and crash through crush traps and boulders.
[*][b]Spider-Spin[/b] lets you charge up a roll that clings to surfaces as you zip around.
[/list]
[h1]The Other Stuff[/h1]
[list][*]I've completely rewritten a [b]certain boss[/b] enemy from scratch, so look forward to that.
[*]I've completely [b]overhauled the way the encyclopedia looks[/b], and added a few new illustrations and entries to it.
[*]I've [b]added a stats screen[/b] on the encyclopedia where you can see things like your best depth, total kills, and most frequently cast spell.[/list]

That's about it for the major new features, but there are also a lot of smaller changes and big bugfixes.

I know, I know, there's no new environment yet, but part of the reason for the level generator rewrite is that as I was working on the Deep Dark I kept running into a lot of things I wanted to do that just weren't supported by the old generator. In any case, I hope it was worth the wait, and now that the generator rewrite is done I'm going to be laser-focusing my attention on adding the [b]midgame boss[/b], the [b]Deep Dark[/b], and bringing back [b]wayward kids[/b] in a way that isn't crashy and buggy and broken.

[h1]The Plea[/h1]
As I'm sure you've noticed, I'm really bad at keeping these here forums up to date on the game's happenings. I'm...super active basically everywhere [i]except[/i] on Steam - especially the [url=https://discord.gg/sRGpPS]Catacomb Kids Discord[/url], and my [url=https://twitter.com/FourbitFriday]Twitter[/url], and my weekly [url=http://twitch.tv/fourbitfriday/]Twitch Dev-streams[/url] - the ones that I've been doing pretty consistently for several years at this point. Even on the [url=https://www.reddit.com/r/catacombkids]Subreddit[/url], when it's not super quiet there. I kind of hate using Steam as both a player and a dev, and frequently forget it exists. I will probably always hate it, especially now that Slack and Discord occupy the space in my life that forums used to.

BUT! Now that I've finally admitted that to you all - and to myself - I figure it's probably only right that rather than continuing to neglect this significant part of the community, doing a great disservice and injustice to all you great many players who have and continue to support the game, I should reach out for help! I'm REALLY BAD AT COMMUNITY MANAGEMENT, but I know there are people who are NOT THAT and would probably be willing to help out with keeping folks here appraised of the game's progress in a way that I never could.

So uh. Yeah. [b]If you're good at community management and want to [i]volunteer[/i][/b] to help make this steam forum an informed and welcoming place to new and old players alike, hit me up at tyriq [at] ckgame [dot] net.

Thanks for stickin' with me. 
Sorry I'm bad at this. 
Hope the update is fun.
I'm not dead yet.

notes.title: New Class - Tinkerer Update!
notes.notes:
So, it's been yet another while and a half, and here we are again. I come bearing gifts. 

Watch this:

https://youtu.be/S0DF43O-3mU

If you don't feel like watching that then read this stuff (it's mostly the same words):

[h1]The Tinkerer![/h1]
First things first, this update adds a new player class to the game; [b]The Tinkerer[/b]. Tinkerers are crafty item-users, planners, and mechanics, and as such they are associated with [b]Intelligence[/b]. Their class ability isn't really an ability so much as a companion: All tinkerers have a flying robot buddy that can carry items and fight alongside them.

The [b]Tinker-Bot[/b] has four different modes that the player can switch between at will:
[list]
[*]In [b]Defensive[/b] mode, the tinker-bot will only attack enemies that you're already in combat with, but won't fly off and start fights on its own.
[*]In [b]Offensive[/b] mode, it'll attack any nearby creature regardless of whether they're aware of you or not.
[*]In [b]Manual[/b] mode, you control the robot directly, letting you move, attack, and pick up items with it, but you lose control of your Kid while doing so.
[*]In [b]Idle[/b] mode, the tinker-bot enters an inactive standby state: You can use this mode to tell the bot to wait somewhere out of the way while you go do something dangerous. You can also interact with the tinkerbot in this mode to manage its held item or modify its behaviour. 
[/list]

Of course, nothing lives forever, and the tinker-bot will be destroyed if it takes too much damage. When this happens it breaks into three pieces that are scattered around the level, and in order to restore it you'll need to reassemble the parts and then take a moment to power it up again. When you repair your bot this way, you'll become mentally exhausted for a couple floors, during which time if it breaks again, repairing it might result in some...lower quality results - or else come at a high cost.

In addition to their tinker-bot companions, Tinkerers also have a chance to start with items unique to their class, called [b]"Contraptions."[/b] There are only two kinds of contraptions so far - [b]Grenades[/b] and [b]Wind-up Turtles[/b] - but more are planned for future updates.

Those are the essentials of the new Tinkerer class, but there's much more to them that you'll have to discover for yourself. I'm excited to finally have the fourth class implemented and I think they'll find their place alongside the bully, wanderer, and poet as a valued addition to the game.

[h1]Catacoins[/h1]
The next major addition to this update is the introduction of [b]Catacoins[/b]. These coins are a kind of currency that you gain over the course of multiple runs by getting far and gaining [b]reputations[/b]. Different reputations are worth different amounts of Catacoins based on how difficult they are to get, but even if you don't get any reputations at all, you'll still slowly gain Catacoins over the course of your runs to spend.

As for what you do with these coins, there's only one thing to spend them on so far, but I think it's pretty neat: You can [b]spend coins to customize the otherwise randomly-rolled Kids[/b], tweaking certain starting traits and equipment to create a kid that suits the way you play, but keep in mind that [b]the more [i]specific[/i] you are, the pricier the kid becomes[/b]. I've also removed the ability to continually re-roll new random kids at no cost: backing out to the menu and going forward again a million times won't get you what you want!

You can choose to spend just a few coins for a simple quality of life improvement, or save them up to roll an expensive all-star suited to your tastes -- but play well, to make sure they survive and make the investment worthwhile.

[h1]Shops[/h1]
I've also made some changes to shopkeepers: They're no longer generic sellers-of-all things, but are instead divided into four different shop types: [b]blacksmiths[/b], [b]magic dealers[/b], [b]potion brewers[/b], and [b]clothiers[/b]. In addition to each shop type offering different kinds of items, shopkeepers themselves now offers a service unique to their profession. 
[list]
[*]Blacksmiths can improve your weapon's stats and repair damaged equipment.
[*]Magic dealers will sell you a single spell that doesn't require learning points to acquire.
[*]Potion brewers will identify any potion type, for a price.
[*]Clothiers offer enchantments for your armor and shoes. 
[/list]

[h1]What's Next?[/h1]
So, now that this new class is out and the groundwork has been laid for meta progression in the form of Catacoins, my next major goals are the implementation of the third environment, the [b]Deep Dark[/b] and the addition of [b]Tier 3 boons[/b], and [b]transitioning development to Game Maker Studio 2[/b]. But like, in the reverse order from what I just said. Of course this all will be aalongside the continued fleshing-out of existing systems - adding more meals and meal effects, more things to purchase with catacoins, more spell overloads and trances, etc.

[h1]I'm Still Not Dead[/h1]
Lastly, as I've mentioned before but will continue to mention for as long as it remains true: If you ever think I'm dead or have dropped off the face of the earth (like I know sometimes happens) Check out my [url=twitch.tv/fourbitfriday]Twitch.tv[/url] on Mondays or Fridays - unless I'm out of town I'll always be dev-streaming from 3-6PM PST. We've also got a relatively active [url=https://discord.gg/6zqWHcZ]discord channel[/url] that y'all're all welcome to party in. But like, not a rowdy party. A really chill low-key one because honestly we're all tired but it's only Monday and we still have to be up tomorrow morning, and it's not even like we don't see each other often anyway, so there's no need to get all wound up when we all know we're just going to be back here again in a couple weeks.

So anyway, sorry this build took such a long time getting out - there were a lot of irritating and common bugs in the last version, and going so long without at least addressing them was pretty unacceptable of me. [b]My bad.[/b] I'll try to do better forever. notes.title: New Class - Tinkerer Update!
notes.notes:
So, it's been yet another while and a half, and here we are again. I come bearing gifts. 

Watch this:

https://youtu.be/S0DF43O-3mU

If you don't feel like watching that then read this stuff (it's mostly the same words):

[h1]The Tinkerer![/h1]
First things first, this update adds a new player class to the game; [b]The Tinkerer[/b]. Tinkerers are crafty item-users, planners, and mechanics, and as such they are associated with [b]Intelligence[/b]. Their class ability isn't really an ability so much as a companion: All tinkerers have a flying robot buddy that can carry items and fight alongside them.

The [b]Tinker-Bot[/b] has four different modes that the player can switch between at will:
[list]
[*]In [b]Defensive[/b] mode, the tinker-bot will only attack enemies that you're already in combat with, but won't fly off and start fights on its own.
[*]In [b]Offensive[/b] mode, it'll attack any nearby creature regardless of whether they're aware of you or not.
[*]In [b]Manual[/b] mode, you control the robot directly, letting you move, attack, and pick up items with it, but you lose control of your Kid while doing so.
[*]In [b]Idle[/b] mode, the tinker-bot enters an inactive standby state: You can use this mode to tell the bot to wait somewhere out of the way while you go do something dangerous. You can also interact with the tinkerbot in this mode to manage its held item or modify its behaviour. 
[/list]

Of course, nothing lives forever, and the tinker-bot will be destroyed if it takes too much damage. When this happens it breaks into three pieces that are scattered around the level, and in order to restore it you'll need to reassemble the parts and then take a moment to power it up again. When you repair your bot this way, you'll become mentally exhausted for a couple floors, during which time if it breaks again, repairing it might result in some...lower quality results - or else come at a high cost.

In addition to their tinker-bot companions, Tinkerers also have a chance to start with items unique to their class, called [b]"Contraptions."[/b] There are only two kinds of contraptions so far - [b]Grenades[/b] and [b]Wind-up Turtles[/b] - but more are planned for future updates.

Those are the essentials of the new Tinkerer class, but there's much more to them that you'll have to discover for yourself. I'm excited to finally have the fourth class implemented and I think they'll find their place alongside the bully, wanderer, and poet as a valued addition to the game.

[h1]Catacoins[/h1]
The next major addition to this update is the introduction of [b]Catacoins[/b]. These coins are a kind of currency that you gain over the course of multiple runs by getting far and gaining [b]reputations[/b]. Different reputations are worth different amounts of Catacoins based on how difficult they are to get, but even if you don't get any reputations at all, you'll still slowly gain Catacoins over the course of your runs to spend.

As for what you do with these coins, there's only one thing to spend them on so far, but I think it's pretty neat: You can [b]spend coins to customize the otherwise randomly-rolled Kids[/b], tweaking certain starting traits and equipment to create a kid that suits the way you play, but keep in mind that [b]the more [i]specific[/i] you are, the pricier the kid becomes[/b]. I've also removed the ability to continually re-roll new random kids at no cost: backing out to the menu and going forward again a million times won't get you what you want!

You can choose to spend just a few coins for a simple quality of life improvement, or save them up to roll an expensive all-star suited to your tastes -- but play well, to make sure they survive and make the investment worthwhile.

[h1]Shops[/h1]
I've also made some changes to shopkeepers: They're no longer generic sellers-of-all things, but are instead divided into four different shop types: [b]blacksmiths[/b], [b]magic dealers[/b], [b]potion brewers[/b], and [b]clothiers[/b]. In addition to each shop type offering different kinds of items, shopkeepers themselves now offers a service unique to their profession. 
[list]
[*]Blacksmiths can improve your weapon's stats and repair damaged equipment.
[*]Magic dealers will sell you a single spell that doesn't require learning points to acquire.
[*]Potion brewers will identify any potion type, for a price.
[*]Clothiers offer enchantments for your armor and shoes. 
[/list]

[h1]What's Next?[/h1]
So, now that this new class is out and the groundwork has been laid for meta progression in the form of Catacoins, my next major goals are the implementation of the third environment, the [b]Deep Dark[/b] and the addition of [b]Tier 3 boons[/b], and [b]transitioning development to Game Maker Studio 2[/b]. Of course this all will be aalongside the continued fleshing-out of existing systems - adding more meals and meal effects, more things to purchase with catacoins, more spell overloads and trances, etc.

Within, you will find undead that roam freely, and grumbul hunters whose excursions have brought them far from their comforts in the Upper Dungeon. Many fun new deaths await in the frigid depths, including but not limited to: being swallowed whole, crushed by giant icicles, spat upon by ghosts, and torn apart by winged beasts while caught in a bear trap and desperately fumbling for a potion. With it being so cold in the Anticropolis, you'll also have to keep an eye on your temperature to make sure you don't suffer from frostbite: Keep dry, dress warmly, and seek fire".

notes.title: Catacomb Kids update introduces the Wanderer
notes.notes:
Really quite good platforming roguelike Catacomb Kids has been making do with just two character classes since it appeared on Early Access a few months ago, so it's about time developers FourbitFriday added another one. They've done just that, obviously, supplementing its Poet and Bully classes with the Wanderer (basically the game's agile hunter class, capable of tracking enemies and using a sort of detective mode to scan the environment). Catacomb Kids is also 20% off on Steam, Itch.io and Humble Bundle (though the discount isn't live there yet) for the next week.

Update 0.0.10 (man, it sounds like there's a long way to go yet) also promises "more deadliness", "better level generation", peg legs, vicious dog enemies and more. My copy of the game has just been automagically updated on Steam, so there's your confirmation that the update has hit. I've had a quick go, and I like the cut of the Wanderer's vision-mode-having jib.

You can read the full patch notes for the update here.

notes.title: 0.0.10 - Wanderer Update!
notes.notes:
[img]http://www.fourbitfriday.com/CatacombKids/ckwander_smaller.png[/img]
[i]Art by Joe Gribbin[/i]

[b]SO[/b].

It's been a minute, eh? A minute and a half, even. That's fine though, because I'm still alive, and this is still happening. [b]That's right![/b] As a beaten, bleeding, heart-still-beating Kid once said; "I'm not dead yet!"

So what have I been up to, you may be asking yourself. Maybe you aren't. How would I know? I'm not your brain. I'll tell you anyway though:

[b]Wandering[/b] is what I've been up to -- as in, making the new Wanderer class. They're speedy and have senses sharp as knives, they do. I hope you enjoy them. As well I've laid the groundwork for [b]unique weapons[/b] and added a few, and made some not insignificant changes to the level generator, not least of which are locked doors and new premade rooms. It may have taken a while but I can say at last that the generator is ready to be iced over and flipped upside down for the coming Anticropolis.

I've also added [b]Alchemy[/b] and [b]Dipper[/b], the two second-tier [b]INT[/b] boons, which marks at last the implementation of all the first two tiers of stat boons. Some of the other boons, spells and skills have also been updated and improved.

notes.title: March Dev Update!
notes.notes:
So, it’s been a little over a month since the Early Access release! 

Q: How’s it going so far?

A: [b]GOOD[/b].

Following the first [b]quick bugfix build[/b] a few days after the initial steam launch, I continued working on fixing bugs and crashes, and easing back into game dev mode after the hectic weeks leading up to Early Access.

Then, March kicked off with the [b]Game Developer’s Conference[/b], where I gave a talk about procedural level generation. People seemed to like it, so that’s cool! Since I had to gather some resources and make slides for that presentation anyway, I’m gonna use that as an excuse/jumping-off point to [b]finally do a write-up about CK’s level generation[/b] that I’ve been talking about making for a while, so look forward to that happening sometime very soon.

At GDC I also met a ton of rad people working on groovy things, like [url=https://twitter.com/moppin_]moppppin[/url], who’s making [url=http://downwellgame.com/]Downwell[/url], and Tim Keenan, who got me excited for [url=http://duskers.misfits-attic.com/]Duskers[/url], and [url=http://nihilocrat.itch.io/]Nihilocrat[/url], who does cool nice things that I dig. And, I mean, there were a ton of other folks. Like wow so many — all doing groovy cool rad things. Jeez, just [b]too many[/b].

--

Anyway, after recovering from GDC and getting that wombat of creativity dug down in my gut again, I got back to The Kids. 

Since the EA release I’ve been keepin’ three eyes on [b]Twitch streamers[/b] and [b]Youtube Let’s Plays[/b] of the game - due in part to narcissism but also so that I can see the areas people are having trouble with, take note of bugs and balance issues, and laugh at their many, many (many, many) deaths. Watching these videos has brought about a few balancing changes, like [b]making enemies hit softer[/b] on the earlier floors, severely shortening the duration of the spell [b]Shadow Cloak[/b], and a few other tweaks and changes to make the game easier or harder in the proper places.

I mean really, [i]why did Shadow Cloak even last that long in the first place?[/i]

--

During the Monday streams, I continued work on [b]Trance[/b], adding another valuable tool to the player’s arsenal. Trance is the [b]counterpart boon[/b] to [b]Overload[/b]: where Overload focuses on making spells more outwardly powerful, Trances are more about imbuing the player with a more passive aspect of the spell. This doesn’t mean that Trances are always merely defensive - though that is a trend they have - but that rather than having an immediate outward effect, they grant the player some [b]trait or ability that persists for a short duration[/b].

I’ve also made [b]Trance[/b] and [b]Overload[/b] require [b]Charge Stars[/b], which was actually the intention for them all along but which I didn’t have finished in time for the release. Essentially, casting a spell as an Overload or Trance will cost a kind of spell charge called a ‘[b]Star[/b]’, and that spell can’t be Overloaded or Trance’d again until its [b]Charge Star[/b] has been recovered. [b]Charge Stars[/b] can be found in [b]fancy chests[/b] and may sometimes be [b]dropped by tougher enemies[/b].

They also make a nice sound when they hit the ground; a consequence of the work [b]Hryx and Doseone[/b] have been doing to make the game sound amazing.

Hey did I mention how [b][i]pumped[/i][/b] I am to have [b]Doseone[/b] working on the game? I don’t think I have, so there’s that. Him and [b]Stevie[/b] have been [i]killin’ it[/i] together aurally for nearly a year now, and I can’t wait to make some headway on the [b]Anticropolis[/b] so you guys can hear the beauty it’s shaping up to be even in these early stages.

Lastly and most recently, I’ve set to work knocking out some of the inefficiencies of the code that had been having a significant impact on performance. Not least among these elements are [b]gasses[/b], which have been [b]completely reworked[/b]. They now are able to spread around corners an be blown around by [b]Whirlwind[/b], in addition to their previous functions. This is also good because gasses will be an important aspect of the [b]Anticropolis[/b], and even moreso the [b]Deep Dark[/b].

--

So that’s how my month has gone. The first [i]real[/i] [b]monthly build update[/b] to the game will happen [b]sometime later this week[/b], and include all of the above changes plus a bunch more, as well as a couple other announcements.

Look forward to it!
